Level-10: Add a JavaFX GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the console-only interface with a chat-style JavaFX window:
scrolling message bubbles, a text field and a Send button, driven by
a new Ben#getResponse method that returns reply text instead of
printing it.

Main holds the UI; Launcher holds main and calls Application.launch so
the app still starts when packaged as a fat JAR. Gradle's mainClass now
points at ben.Launcher. Ben#run and the console entry point are kept.

JavaFX is provided by the bundled fx-zulu JDK, so no new Gradle
dependency is needed.

A-Jar: Declare JavaFX as a dependency, not the JDK
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously ben.jar relied on the active JDK being an FX-flavoured build
(Zulu FX) for JavaFX classes, so shadowJar had nothing JavaFX-related to
package and the jar was only 20KB. Add the org.openjfx Gradle plugin and
declare javafx.controls (the only module the GUI uses) as a real
dependency, so shadowJar bundles the actual JavaFX jars in. This makes
ben.jar runnable via 'java -jar' on any JDK, and brings the jar to ~8MB,
meeting the Week 5 release requirement.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Assertions: Use assertions for internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Several places in the code rely on invariants that should always hold
given the surrounding logic (e.g. every switch branch in
Task.deserialize assigns a value before it's used, and String.split
with a limit of 2 can only ever return 1 or 2 elements) but were never
actually checked, so a future edit that broke one of them would fail
silently or with a confusing NPE far from the real cause.

Let's add assert statements at these points to document and check the
invariants during development and testing, where the cost of the check
is worth it. These are not user-input validation (that stays as
BenException, which must run in production); assertions are for bugs
in the program itself. Also enable assertions on the 'run' Gradle task
to match 'test', which already runs with them on by default.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CodeQuality: Remove duplicated formatting logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Ben.formatList() and findTasks() built their numbered listings with
near-identical code, and addTask()/deleteTask() each recomputed the
same 'N task(s) in the list' pluralization inline. Parser.parseEvent()
also threw the same 'needs /from and /to' message from two places.
Any future change to how a list or count is worded would have needed
updating multiple copies in sync, an easy way to introduce a mismatch.

Let's extract formatNumberedList() and taskCountLine() in Ben, and hoist
the repeated error message into a local constant in Parser, so each
piece of wording exists once. Output is unchanged; verified by running
the existing test suite and a manual console session covering list,
find, add and delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Streams: Use streams for the two simple filter/map loops
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.find() and Storage.save() were plain for-loops doing a
straightforward filter and a straightforward map respectively, with no
side effects other than building the result list.

Let's rewrite both as streams (filter+collect, and map+collect), which
says directly what each loop is doing instead of making the reader
trace index-by-index mutation of an accumulator. Storage.load() is left
as a loop: it catches a checked BenException per line to skip corrupted
entries, which does not translate cleanly into a stream lambda.
Behaviour verified unchanged via the existing test suite and a manual
add/save/find round trip.

commitResults.messageTitle: BCD-Extension: Add tagging (C-Tagging)
commitResults.messageBody:
Ben has no way to attach freeform metadata to a task beyond its type
and one date/time field, so there is no way to group or annotate tasks
by anything the built-in fields do not cover, e.g. 'urgent' or
'errand'.

Let's let a task carry any number of '#tag' style tags, addable either
inline when the task is created ('todo buy milk #errand') or after the
fact via a new 'tag INDEX name' command. Displaying and saving tags
consistently at the end of a task regardless of type needed toString()
and serialize() to stop being overridden ad hoc per subclass, so both
are now template methods in Task with extraInfo()/extraFields() hooks;
Deadline and Event plug into those instead of calling super. Old save
files without a tags field still load correctly, since that field is
optional on read.

Verified via the existing test suite plus manual checks of inline
tagging, the tag command, duplicate tags, error handling, and loading
an old-format save file.
